newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares slide, sentiment seen bearish.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares slide, sentiment seen bearish.

text.p: Austria's ATX index ended slightly lower on Tuesday, aided late in the session by a spate of U.S. data, but traders were bearish about the chance of a pick-up in the market in the near term.
Traders said a sharp drop in U.S. March durable goods orders and good news on U.S. wages triggered a late flurry of buying, driving the index off earlier lows.
But the rise was artificial, said one. "The mood is basically bearish."
"It was disappointing that we stayed below 1,200 points," said another.
Dealers were pinning hopes on the bond market for support as they did not expect the bourse to benefit from bullish international leads.
"Tomorrow we'll see whether we follow today's upswing in the United States," said one.
The ATX index dropped 0.37 percent, or 4.4 points, to 1,198.17. Among its constituents 11 ATX shares fell, seven rose and three were unchanged.
Microchip maker AMS led the decliners, toppling 2.17 percent to 900 schillings after reporting first quarter losses.
Regional utility EVN and high-grade steelmaker Boehler also came under pressure.
The top gainer was Bank Austria preferred shares, climbing 1.78 percent to 400 schillings.

Motorcycle maker KTM, not included in the ATX but continuously traded, up 2.65 percent at 735 schillings on follow-through buying after the company on Monday announced a strong set of first half earnings and an upbeat forecast for the full year.
The May ATX future gained 2.5 points to 1,194 on turnover of 659 contracts.
